DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dil . ov. h OILG OPINION NO. FEB 23 MARIA REMEDIOS CHUA-SY, DMD jhingsy@yahoo.com Dear Ms. Chua-Sy: This has reference to your electronic mail dated 24 September 2023 seeking legal opinion from this Department regarding the refusal of a certain Barangay to furnish complainant of own blotter report. Per your representation, you filed a blotter report with your barangay against your neighbor for an incident that allegedly involved threats, slander and interference in an ongoing trimming of your tree inside your property since the leaves and small branches were encroaching your property. You then represented that you asked for a receiving copy of the blotter report but the barangay official refused stating that this Department prohibits the issuance of a copy of the blotter report. That you were perplexed since you were the complainant on record, and that it is a matter of right that you should have a receiving copy. However, you represented that the person-in-charge insisted that this Department ordered them not to give said copy, and that they will only release said copy if they are ordered by proper courts. Thus, the request for legal opinion on the following: I. Whether or not the DILG ordered not to issue a copy of the blotter report unless it is ordered by the proper tribunal; 2. Is there an existing Memorandum Circular to that effect? Since the queries are interrelated, we deem it proper to answer them in one (1) discussion. At the outset, please be apprised that barangay blotter reports are considered public records and are maintained by local barangay officials for transparency and community safety purposes. Barangay blotter is merely a report of an incident which contains material details involving violation of rules, laws, and ordinances reported. However, the specific rules and procedures for accessing barangay blotter reports may vary by location and jurisdiction within the Philippines. "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Barangay officials or personnel from the barangay where the incident or report was filed should be able to assist you with your request; however, depending on the barangay's laws/ordinances and processes, you may be required to submit your identification as well as a cause for seeking the report. Relative thereto, please be informed that this Department has not issued any Memorandum Circular requiring a court order before issuing a copy of the barangay blotter report to the parties. The opinion of this Department is based solely on the facts and representations you have narrated in your letter and our appreciation of the same. We hope to have addressed your concern accordingly. Thank you. Very truly yours, BY ORITY OF THE SECRETARY: AN CTOR R. LLAMAS Und ecretary for External, Legal and Legislative Affairs and co rrent OIC, LLLS OUSELLNJVRULLLS-LRALLD/lasm Page 2 of 2
